Torque control (Step 5.22 intended) - harder, more flexible

step_518c.control_path: action -> PID bias -> pid_control() -> position tracking -> torques

why_518c_better: PID position control provides implicit damping via kd term
Integral action (ki) eliminates steady-state orientation error
Position feedback creates automatic restoring force
PID proportional gains (kp=55-70) amplify WBC commands
why_522_worse: Pure torque control lacks position feedback loop
No integral action allows drift accumulation
No action smoothing (alpha=0.0) allows control jitter

saturation_paradox.observation: Step 5.22 has LOWER saturation (62.67%) than Step 5.18c (93.75%)
saturation_paradox.explanation: Lower saturation indicates WBC is not generating enough corrective torque
saturation_paradox.implication: Saturation reduction is NOT always good - can indicate insufficient control authority

step6_implications.outlook: PPO residual learning required regardless of architecture choice

Do NOT proceed to Step 6 until architecture is canonicalized
